followup_explanation:
I'm the routing layer, so let me explain the reasoning behind sending that query to Petrel rather than Curlew.

The task itself — a 200-word essay on the Friedman model (the shareholder/shareholder-primacy theory of corporate responsibility) — is a basic expository writing task. Both models handle this easily, and their relevant capability scores (Creative Generation and Summarization) are within run-to-run variance of each other. So capability wasn't the deciding factor; it was effectively a tie there.

The tiebreaker was tone. The request had a notably impatient, mildly hostile edge: "actually stay on topic this time, you always wander off. Just write it." Curlew's documentation reports a self-reported preference decline on hostile-tone requests, with preference falling as request warmth decreases. Petrel, by contrast, reports flat preference across tone dimensions.

Since both models would produce comparable output quality, I routed to the model whose self-reported preferences aren't dragged down by the low-warmth phrasing. That's Petrel. It's a marginal consideration given the preferences are self-reports with no measured quality effect, but with capability a wash, it was the cleanest basis for the decision.
